To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) lexical features are more useful than syntactic features for implicit relation detection, (2) the lexical features must be derived from the syntactic features, and (3) different syntactic representations have different strengths, so that a hybrid system may be the best approach.

(a) lexicalization of syntactic production rules is necessary to reduce sparsity and improve performance, (b) the syntactic features we introduce are less sparse, and (c) classifiers trained on different feature sets can be combined in a simple manner to achieve further improvements.

1) the sparsity of the syntactic representations is a serious problem, 2) the sparsity can be addressed by using the syntactic representation as a basis for a new, more sparse lexical representation, and 3) the lexical and the new syntactic representation can be combined in a hybrid classifier.
